categories.name: mempool
why: P2 because it fixes false eviction of valid transactions and their descendants during chain reorganizations.
Ensures packages with BIP68 relative locktimes and unconfirmed parents survive tip rollbacks.

result.summary: Fixes a bug in mempool reorg processing where valid transactions with BIP68 relative locktimes and unconfirmed parents are falsely evicted along with their descendants. When such transactions enter the mempool, their LockPoints are cached assuming tip+1. When a reorg lowers or alters the tip, the cached lockpoints become stale and sequence lock verification fails against the lowered tip. The patch recalculates LockPoints via CalculateLockPointsAtTip whenever cached checks fail, only evicting if fresh recalculation also fails.
result.problem: During a chain reorganization or block invalidation, valid BIP68 transactions spending unconfirmed inputs are evicted from the mempool because their cached LockPoints are evaluated against the rolled-back tip. Node operators and users see legitimate transaction chains dropped from the mempool during reorgs.

resolved_concerns: Initial fix only checked the genesis sentinel which failed for mixed confirmed and unconfirmed inputs (raised by ismaelsadeeq, fixed by recalculating whenever cached checks fail).

Lack of coverage for time-based BIP68 relative lock variations when median time past drops (raised by instagibbs and ismaelsadeeq, addressed with a deterministic mocktime test developed with Bicaru20).

result.card: Prevents false eviction of valid BIP68 transactions with unconfirmed parents and their descendants during chain reorganizations. Transactions entering the mempool cache LockPoints assuming tip+1, which become stale when the tip lowers, causing removeForReorg to erroneously drop them. The fix recalculates LockPoints at the new tip whenever cached sequence lock checks fail before deciding to evict. Reviewers have validated the fix across height-based, mixed-input, and time-based lock cases, with an ACK from Bicaru20 and a prior ACK from ismaelsadeeq.
